narrative.title: Sending the Relay Back Down the Line
narrative.scenario: A one-way relay line must suddenly run in reverse — every worker's outbound link is re-aimed at the person who used to point at them, and the last worker becomes the new starter. Each rewiring happens one worker at a time while walking the line, and nobody may lose track of the worker ahead while their own link is being flipped.
narrative.inputFormat: An array head of node values representing the linked list.
narrative.outputFormat: The values of the reversed list, read from the new head.

testCases.explanation: Every link flips and the tail node 5 opens the reversed chain.
A two-node chain needs exactly one link flip.

hintLevels: Level 1: Reversal is relinking, not revaluing — the nodes stay put, only their arrows change direction.
Level 2: Keep three trackers: the node behind (already reversed), the current node, and the node ahead; flip the current node's arrow toward the behind, then slide all three forward.
Level 3: The saved-ahead pointer is what stops the rest of the list from being orphaned the instant you flip — and the tracker that ends on null is the new head.
